items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy-linked affair probe
items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down after admitting a romantic relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence says was recruited by China's top spy agency. The departure of the AI chip giant's co-founder marks a seismic shift in the AI economy's power structure.

items.headline: Fed survey: 87% of contacts cite AI as financial stability risk
items.summary: A new Federal Reserve survey found 87% of contacts flagged AI as a salient financial stability risk, with advanced computing-related debt issuance surging to $680 billion by October 2026. The findings underscore growing concern about an AI-driven debt bubble.

items.headline: Anthropic targets up to $69.3 billion blockbuster IPO
items.summary: Anthropic's latest draft prospectus set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, aiming to raise as much as $69.3 billion in one of the largest IPOs ever. The company reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, a more than 1,200% year-over-year jump.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
items.summary: Anthropic released two new frontier models — Fable 5.2 for coding and agents, Mythos 5.2 for restricted cybersecurity and life-sciences work — generating outputs up to 30% faster at lower prices. It's the company's first frontier release since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow the pace of AI development in September.

items.headline: Anthropic inks $3.4 billion gas-powered data center deal
items.summary: Anthropic acquired energy generation equipment in the largest deal of its kind to secure AI compute autonomy ahead of its estimated $1.3 trillion IPO. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, and consumers, touting state-of-the-art cybersecurity and improved agentic coding. The launch came just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon as Google intensifies competition with OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.headline: AI safety groups sue five leading AI companies
items.summary: A coalition of online safety and consumer advocacy groups sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and others in San Francisco, seeking to halt further development over 'catastrophic' harm risks. The suit follows a midterm election that handed Democrats control of Congress amid calls to regulate AI.

items.headline: Zimbabwean author cleared of AI use in prize-winning story
items.summary: Author Simbarashe Kundizeza was cleared of allegations that he used AI to write his prize-winning story. The case highlights ongoing disputes over authenticity and AI detection in creative writing competitions.

items.headline: Mercor valued at $20 billion in latest funding round
items.summary: AI training startup Mercor reached a $20 billion valuation in its latest raise, reflecting investor appetite for data-labeling and model-training infrastructure. AI-driven startups raised $102 billion — 64% of global venture capital — in Q3 2026.

items.headline: Peec AI doubles revenue to $20M ARR in six months
items.summary: Berlin-based AI search platform Peec AI passed $20 million in annual recurring revenue less than two years after launch, doubling from $10M ARR in May. More than 4,000 customers across 80+ countries now use it to analyze brand visibility in AI systems.

items.headline: Anthropic buys one-person AI-powered biotech startup
items.summary: Anthropic acquired a solo-founder, AI-powered biotech company, raising questions about whether this signals the future of drug discovery. The deal highlights how AI labs are extending into scientific research applications.

items.headline: Anthropic launches its own AI-powered office suite
items.summary: Anthropic rolled out an AI-powered office suite, following Google and OpenAI into integrated productivity tools. The move puts Claude in direct competition with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace for enterprise work.

items.headline: Enterprises say AI regulation won't stop corporate innovation
items.summary: Corporate technology leaders told WSJ they are pressing ahead with AI plans regardless of regulation solidifying under Democratic control of Congress. Democrats are expected to focus on safety guardrails, including pre-release model testing.

items.headline: Three men indicted for AI voice fraud stealing $129 million
items.summary: A federal indictment alleges three men used generative AI to clone the voices of CEOs and lawyers, defrauding companies of more than $129 million. The case illustrates the escalating threat of AI-enabled impersonation scams.

items.headline: OpenAI adds ChatGPT Wallet for card-free payments
items.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, letting users store a debit or credit card for payments without re-entering card information. The feature deepens ChatGPT's push into commerce and agentic transactions.

items.headline: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion ABB Robotics takeover
items.summary: Chinese authorities halted the sale of ABB Robotics to SoftBank amid wider scrutiny of global transactions affecting Beijing's technology ambitions. China is ABB's largest robotics market, making the block a significant impediment to foreign deals.

items.headline: AI Futures Project pushes intelligence explosion forecast to 2027
items.summary: The AI Futures Project revised its 'intelligence explosion' forecast, with milestones once pegged to 2026 now slipping into May 2027. A February grading found quantitative progress running at roughly 65% of the predicted pace.

items.headline: Cohere brings Embed 5 and Rerank 5 to OpenRouter
items.summary: Cohere made its Embed 5 and Rerank 5 models available on OpenRouter, broadening access to its retrieval and ranking tools. The release targets developers building RAG and search applications.

items.headline: xAI enables default watermarking on Grok text outputs
items.summary: Starting November 7, xAI turned on watermarking by default for text outputs across its Grok model lineup, including grok-4.7, with per-model opt-out available. The move addresses provenance and authenticity concerns across its APIs.
